questions.topic: Composition levy — no collection and no ITC
questions.q: A registered person validly paying tax under the composition scheme makes a taxable domestic supply. Which treatment is required by Section 10(4) of the CGST Act?
o: He may collect GST but cannot claim ITC
He may claim ITC but must not collect GST
He must neither collect tax from the recipient nor claim input tax credit
He may collect GST only where the buyer is unregistered
questions.e: Section 10(4) imposes both restrictions together: a composition taxpayer cannot collect tax from recipients on supplies and cannot take input tax credit. The composition rate is paid by the supplier under the scheme.
tags: Composition levy — no collection and no ITC

questions.topic: Time of supply of goods — forward charge
questions.q: A normal taxable supply of goods is made under forward charge. Ignoring special cases, which event determines the time of supply under Section 12(2)?
o: The date the recipient files GSTR-3B
The earlier of the invoice date (or last date on which it must be issued) and receipt of payment
The date the goods reach the recipient's warehouse in every case
The date on which the supplier files the annual return
questions.e: Section 12(2) generally uses the earlier of the invoice date or the last date on which the invoice is required to be issued, and the date the supplier receives payment. The rule identifies when liability arises, not the return-filing date.

questions.q: A complete refund application is received under Section 54(1), and a refund is ordered under Section 54(5), but the amount is not paid within sixty days. Under Section 56, when does interest generally begin?
o: Only from the end of the financial year
From the day immediately after expiry of sixty days until the refund is made
Only after the taxpayer files an appeal
questions.e: Section 56 provides for interest where a refund ordered under Section 54(5) is not made within sixty days from receipt of the application under Section 54(1). Interest generally runs from the day immediately after that sixty-day period until the refund is made.

questions.topic: Value of supply — transaction value condition
questions.q: Two unrelated businesses enter into a taxable supply agreement. The stated price is the sole consideration and no special valuation rule applies. Which amount is ordinarily the transaction value under Section 15(1)?
o: The price actually paid or payable for the supply
The highest price charged by any competing supplier
questions.e: Section 15(1) starts with the transaction value: the price actually paid or payable, provided the supplier and recipient are not related and price is the sole consideration. Prescribed valuation rules apply when those conditions are not met.

questions.q: A supplier charges the buyer separately for packing and commission in connection with a taxable supply before delivery. How are those charges generally treated under Section 15(2)?
o: They are always excluded because they are shown separately
They are included in the value of supply
They are treated only as exempt income
They reduce the taxable value as a discount
questions.e: Section 15(2)(c) includes incidental expenses such as commission and packing charged by the supplier at or before delivery or supply of the service. Separate presentation on an invoice does not by itself make them excludable.

questions.topic: Wrong tax classification — intra-State treated as inter-State
questions.q: A registered supplier pays CGST and State GST on a transaction believed to be intra-State. It is later held to be an inter-State supply. What relief is provided by Section 77(1) of the CGST Act?
o: The supplier keeps both taxes as input credit
The recipient receives a cash refund automatically
The supplier is refunded the central and State taxes so paid, subject to prescribed procedure
The transaction is permanently treated as intra-State
questions.e: Section 77(1) addresses a registered person who paid central and State tax on a transaction considered intra-State but later held to be inter-State. The person is entitled to refund of the taxes so paid in the prescribed manner and subject to conditions.

questions.q: A company purchases a five-seat passenger car for the general use of its directors. It is not used for further supply of vehicles, passenger transportation or driving instruction. What is the normal Section 17(5)(a) position?
o: Full input tax credit is automatically available
Credit is available only if the car is purchased in cash
Credit is available only when the car is used outside the State
questions.e: Section 17(5)(a) generally blocks ITC on a motor vehicle for transportation of persons with approved seating capacity of not more than thirteen, including the driver, unless a specified exception applies. General director use is not one of those exceptions.

questions.q: A person who is not registered under GST issues a bill showing an amount as CGST on a taxable supply. Which statutory principle applies?
o: An unregistered person may collect tax if the amount is small
An unregistered person may collect tax if the buyer agrees
The amount automatically becomes input tax credit
An unregistered person must not collect an amount by way of tax under the CGST Act
questions.e: Section 32(1) prohibits a person who is not registered from collecting an amount by way of tax under the CGST Act. A buyer's consent or the small size of the amount does not create registration or collection authority.

questions.topic: Tax invoice — separate indication of tax
questions.q: A taxable supply is made for consideration. What does Section 33 require the person liable to pay tax to do in the relevant assessment and supply documents?
o: Hide the tax component inside the price in every document
Prominently indicate the amount of tax forming part of the price
Show only the supplier's profit margin
Mention tax only in the annual return
questions.e: Section 33 requires the amount of tax forming part of the price to be prominently indicated in assessment documents, the tax invoice and other like documents. This supports transparency about the tax component of the transaction.

questions.e: Section 59 places the self-assessment responsibility on every registered person. The person must assess the tax payable under the Act and furnish the return for each tax period as required by Section 39.

questions.topic: Provisional assessment — uncertainty of value or rate
questions.q: A taxable person cannot determine the correct value of a supply or the applicable tax rate. What is the statutory first step to seek provisional assessment under Section 60(1)?
o: Wait until the annual audit is completed
Ask the recipient to choose a rate
Make a written request to the proper officer, explaining the reasons
questions.e: Section 60(1) allows a taxable person who cannot determine the value or applicable rate to request provisional assessment in writing, giving reasons. The proper officer may then specify the provisional value or rate subject to statutory conditions.

Best-judgment assessment using relevant available or gathered material
questions.e: Section 62 addresses registered persons who do not file the required return even after notice under Section 46. The proper officer may determine liability to the best of judgment using relevant material available or gathered.

questions.e: Section 64 permits summary assessment in certain special cases to protect revenue, but the proper officer must first obtain permission from an Additional Commissioner or Joint Commissioner. It is an exceptional assessment route, not the routine scrutiny process.

questions.q: During GST adjudication, the person receiving the notice makes a written request for a hearing. What does Section 75(4) require?
o: An opportunity of hearing must be granted
The request must be rejected if the amount is small
The officer must decide only from the return
The matter must automatically go to the High Court
questions.e: Section 75(4) requires an opportunity of hearing where the person to whom notice was issued requests it in writing. It also requires a hearing where an adverse decision is contemplated against that person.

questions.topic: Adjudication — limits of the final order
questions.q: A show-cause notice proposes a tax demand of ₹2 lakh on stated grounds. The adjudication order confirms ₹3 lakh on a new ground not mentioned in the notice. Which Section 75(7) principle is violated?
o: An order must always be lower than the tax invoice
The order cannot demand more than the amount specified in the notice or confirm a demand on grounds outside the notice
The officer must use the electronic cash ledger
A demand can be confirmed only after an annual return
questions.e: Section 75(7) limits the adjudication order to the amount specified in the notice and prohibits confirming a demand on grounds other than those specified in the notice. The notice therefore defines the boundaries of the demand adjudication.

questions.topic: Tax collected but not paid — Section 76
questions.q: A person collects ₹18,000 from a customer as an amount representing GST but does not deposit it with the Government. What does Section 76 generally require?
o: The person may retain it until the annual audit
The amount becomes the customer's ITC automatically
The collected amount must be paid forthwith to the Government
The amount is treated as a discount
questions.e: Section 76 requires a person who has collected an amount representing tax and has not paid it to the Government to pay that amount forthwith. The rule prevents a person from retaining money collected from another person as tax.

questions.e: Article 315 provides for the Union Public Service Commission and a Public Service Commission for each State, subject to the constitutional arrangements that allow a Joint State Public Service Commission. It is the constitutional foundation for public service commissions.

questions.q: Which article sets out the functions of Union and State Public Service Commissions, including conducting examinations for appointments to services?
questions.e: Article 320 describes the functions of Public Service Commissions. These include conducting examinations for appointments to services and advising on specified recruitment, promotion and disciplinary matters, subject to constitutional provisions and applicable rules.

questions.q: A citizen is otherwise eligible for inclusion in an electoral roll. Which constitutional article bars exclusion from a general electoral roll solely on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex?
questions.e: Article 325 provides one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency and prohibits exclusion from that roll or a claim to a special electoral roll solely on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.

questions.q: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People is principally provided under which article?
questions.e: Article 330 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People. Article 332 deals with reservation in State Legislative Assemblies, so the two provisions must not be confused.

questions.e: Article 335 directs that the claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes be taken into consideration in appointments to services and posts, consistently with the maintenance of efficiency of administration. It is not a general reservation provision for every category.

Each District Council independently creates the list

The State Public Service Commission issues the list

questions.topic: Seismology — P waves and S waves
questions.q: Seismic records from an earthquake show that a wave has travelled through the Earth's liquid outer core. Which type of body wave can do this?
questions.e: Primary waves are compressional body waves and can travel through solids, liquids and gases. Secondary waves are shear waves and cannot travel through liquids, which is why P-wave and S-wave behaviour helps scientists infer Earth's internal structure.
tags: Seismology — P waves and S waves

questions.q: On a synoptic weather map, what do isobars join?
questions.e: Isobars are lines joining places that have the same atmospheric pressure at a specified time. Their spacing and pattern help meteorologists interpret pressure gradients and likely wind conditions.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure wind speed at a weather station?
questions.e: An anemometer measures wind speed. A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, a hygrometer measures humidity and a rain gauge measures precipitation, so the instruments should not be interchanged.

questions.q: A ridge separates streams that flow into two different river systems. What is this boundary called?
questions.e: A watershed divide is the elevated boundary separating neighbouring drainage basins. Rain falling on opposite sides of the divide generally drains towards different river systems.

questions.q: A river network resembles the branches of a tree and develops over relatively uniform rock with little structural control. Which drainage pattern is this?
questions.e: A dendritic drainage pattern resembles tree branches. It commonly develops where the underlying rock has relatively uniform resistance and there is no strong structural control forcing streams into parallel or right-angled courses.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI

questions.q: A river meander is cut off from the main channel after erosion and deposition narrow its neck. What landform may remain?
questions.e: An oxbow lake forms when a river cuts through the narrow neck of a meander and abandons the loop. The isolated curved water body is a depositional and erosional feature of a meandering river system.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI

questions.q: When are spring tides generally produced?
o: Only at the first and third quarter moons
Only when the Moon is at its farthest distance from Earth
When the Sun, Earth and Moon are approximately aligned at new moon or full moon
questions.e: Spring tides occur around new moon and full moon when the gravitational effects of the Sun and Moon act along approximately the same line. The tidal range is greater than during neap tides.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI

questions.q: During a clear daytime, a coastal area experiences a breeze blowing from the sea towards the land. What is the main cause?
o: The sea heats faster than the land
The Coriolis force reverses direction every afternoon
The land remains cooler than the sea throughout the day
Land heats faster, air rises over it and cooler air moves inland from the sea
questions.e: Land generally warms faster than the sea during the day. Air over the warmer land rises, creating relatively lower pressure near the surface, and cooler air flows from the sea towards the land as a sea breeze.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI

questions.q: A hot surface warms moist air, which rises, expands and cools until condensation produces showers. Which rainfall mechanism is described?
questions.e: Convectional rainfall begins when surface heating causes warm, moist air to rise. As it expands and cools, water vapour condenses into clouds and may produce heavy showers or thunderstorms.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI

questions.q: A rock contains relatively large interlocking crystals because molten material cooled slowly beneath the Earth's surface. How is it classified?
questions.e: Intrusive igneous rocks form when magma cools slowly below the surface. Slow cooling gives crystals more time to grow, producing a coarse-grained texture, as in granite.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Class XI.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.topic: National income — GVA and GDP relationship
questions.q: At market prices, how is GDP related to Gross Value Added at basic prices in the standard national-accounts identity?
o: GDP equals GVA minus all wages
GDP equals GVA plus depreciation only
GDP equals GVA plus product taxes minus product subsidies
questions.e: The standard relationship is GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies. Product taxes raise the market-price measure, while product subsidies are deducted to avoid overstating the market value.
tags: National income — GVA and GDP relationship
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics, Class XII.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes the Consumer Price Index from the Wholesale Price Index?
o: CPI tracks prices faced by consumers, while WPI tracks prices at the wholesale level
questions.e: The Consumer Price Index measures changes in prices of a basket relevant to consumers and is used to assess retail inflation. The Wholesale Price Index tracks price movements at the wholesale stage and has a different coverage and purpose.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics, Class XII.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics, Class XII

questions.q: In the standard Balance of Payments framework, which item is recorded in the capital account rather than the current account?
o: Capital transfers and acquisition or disposal of non-produced non-financial assets
questions.e: The capital account records capital transfers and transactions in non-produced, non-financial assets. Goods, services, primary income and secondary income are recorded in the current account, while most financial investment flows are recorded in the financial account.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Foreign Exchange Reserves and Handbook of Statistics.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Foreign Exchange Reserves and Handbook of Statistics

questions.q: Under a flexible exchange-rate system, the market-driven fall in the value of a currency is generally called:
questions.e: Depreciation is a fall in a currency's value arising from market forces under a flexible exchange-rate system. Devaluation usually refers to an official downward adjustment by the monetary authority under a fixed or managed parity arrangement.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics, Class XII.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics, Class XII

questions.q: A deposit offers a nominal annual interest rate of 7%, while annual inflation is 4%. Using the common approximation, what is the real interest rate?
questions.e: The approximate real interest rate is the nominal interest rate minus the inflation rate. Here, 7% − 4% = 3%. The exact Fisher relationship is multiplicative, but the subtraction is the standard approximation for modest rates.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics, Class XII.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics, Class XII

questions.q: Tax revenue rises by 12% while nominal GDP rises by 8%. Using the standard tax-buoyancy ratio, what is the buoyancy?
questions.e: Tax buoyancy is the ratio of the percentage growth in tax revenue to the percentage growth in the corresponding tax base, commonly nominal GDP. Here it is 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5, meaning tax revenue grew one and a half times as fast as the base.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Department of Economic Affairs — FRBM Report, Estimation of Tax Buoyancies.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Department of Economic Affairs — FRBM Report, Estimation of Tax Buoyancies

questions.q: For a given period, a country's merchandise imports are ₹12 lakh crore and merchandise exports are ₹10 lakh crore. What does this indicate?
o: A merchandise trade deficit of ₹2 lakh crore
A merchandise trade surplus of ₹2 lakh crore
A current-account surplus of ₹22 lakh crore
questions.e: A merchandise trade deficit occurs when the value of merchandise imports exceeds merchandise exports. Here the deficit is ₹12 lakh crore − ₹10 lakh crore = ₹2 lakh crore; this alone does not determine the entire current-account balance.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Foreign Exchange Reserves and Handbook of Statistics.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Foreign Exchange Reserves and Handbook of Statistics

questions.q: Which set correctly lists the main components of India's official foreign exchange reserves?
o: Only US-dollar cash held by commercial banks
Foreign currency assets, gold, Special Drawing Rights and the reserve position in the IMF
Only government securities issued in India
Only export earnings held by private companies
questions.e: The Reserve Bank's foreign-exchange-reserve presentation includes foreign currency assets, gold, Special Drawing Rights and India's reserve tranche position in the IMF. It is not limited to dollars or to private exporters' balances.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Foreign Exchange Reserves and Handbook of Statistics.

questions.q: Two atoms have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. What is their correct relationship?
o: They are ions of different elements
They are isotopes of the same element
They are molecules of the same compound
questions.e: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers because they contain different numbers of neutrons. Their chemical properties are broadly similar because they have the same proton and electron arrangement in neutral atoms.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science, Class X.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science, Class X

questions.q: In terms of electron transfer, which statement correctly defines oxidation?
questions.e: Oxidation is loss of electrons, while reduction is gain of electrons. The two processes occur together in a redox reaction because electrons lost by one species are gained by another.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science, Class X.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science, Class X

questions.q: What happens during electrolysis of an electrolyte?
o: Electrical energy drives a non-spontaneous chemical change
A catalyst changes the reaction rate without current
A liquid changes to gas only by heating
A neutral atom becomes an isotope
questions.e: Electrolysis uses an external electric current to drive a chemical reaction that would not proceed spontaneously under the same conditions. It is used in processes such as electroplating and the decomposition of compounds.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science, Class X.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science, Class X

questions.q: Which statement best describes the role of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
o: It permanently increases the amount of product by changing the equilibrium constant
It changes the reaction rate by providing an alternative pathway and is not consumed overall
It must become the main product
It always raises the temperature of the reaction
questions.e: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a different activation energy and changes the reaction rate. It is regenerated in the overall reaction and does not change the equilibrium constant of the reaction.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science, Class X.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science, Class X

questions.q: Which structure is regarded as the structural and functional unit of the human kidney?
questions.e: The nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney. It filters blood at the renal corpuscle and modifies the filtrate through selective reabsorption and secretion along the renal tubule to help form urine.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology, Class XII.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Biology, Class XII

questions.q: Which part of the inner ear converts mechanical sound vibrations into electrical nerve signals?
questions.e: The cochlea contains sensory hair cells that convert mechanical vibrations into electrical signals carried by the auditory nerve. The semicircular canals are mainly involved in balance rather than hearing.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology, Class XII.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Biology, Class XII

questions.q: The main purpose of vaccination is to:
o: Stimulate the immune system to develop a protective response and memory
Destroy every microorganism in the body immediately
questions.e: Vaccines expose the immune system to an antigen or instructions for producing an antigen, allowing it to develop a protective response and immunological memory. This prepares the body to respond more effectively to later exposure.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology, Class XII.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Biology, Class XII

questions.q: Why are ordinary antibacterial antibiotics not effective against influenza viruses?
o: Influenza viruses have thicker cell walls than bacteria
Viruses lack the bacterial structures and processes targeted by antibacterial antibiotics
Influenza is caused by a fungus
questions.e: Antibacterial antibiotics act on bacterial structures or processes, such as cell-wall synthesis or bacterial ribosomes. Influenza is caused by a virus, so antibiotics do not treat the viral infection itself and should not be used without a bacterial indication.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science, Class X.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science, Class X

questions.q: An office clerk sends one email to several external recipients but does not want recipients to see one another's addresses. Which email field is appropriate?
questions.e: BCC means blind carbon copy. Addresses placed in BCC are not displayed to other ordinary recipients, making it useful when sending a message to a group whose members should not see one another's email addresses.

questions.q: A clerk has thousands of transaction rows and wants a quick summary of total payments by district and month without changing the source data. Which spreadsheet feature is most suitable?
questions.e: A PivotTable summarises and reorganises a larger table by fields such as district and month. It can calculate totals, counts and other summaries without manually rewriting the underlying transaction records.

questions.q: A spreadsheet should automatically highlight overdue dates in red whenever a date meets a specified rule. Which feature should be used?
questions.e: Conditional formatting applies a visual format automatically when cell values satisfy a rule. It is suitable for highlighting overdue dates, duplicates or values outside a defined range without manually colouring each cell.

questions.q: A data-entry sheet must allow only dates within a specified financial year in a particular column. Which feature is designed to restrict such entries?
questions.e: Data validation restricts the type or range of values users may enter into spreadsheet cells. A date rule can limit entries to a specified period and reduce inconsistent or invalid data in office registers.

questions.q: In presentation software, which feature controls common fonts, logos, placeholders and layout elements across multiple slides?
questions.e: The Slide Master controls the shared design and layout elements used by slides in a presentation. Changing the master can update consistent fonts, logos, colours and placeholders without editing each slide separately.

questions.q: Which description best matches a CSV file?
o: A database backup that can only be opened by one vendor
A plain-text table format in which fields are separated by delimiters, commonly commas
questions.e: CSV stands for comma-separated values. It stores tabular data as plain text, with records on separate lines and fields separated by commas or another specified delimiter, making it useful for data exchange between applications.

questions.q: Which file format is specifically designed as a PDF profile for long-term electronic document preservation?
questions.e: PDF/A is an archival-oriented PDF standard designed to preserve documents over the long term. It restricts certain features that may depend on external resources and requires reliable embedding of important document components such as fonts.

questions.q: Which file extension is used by default for a modern Excel workbook that is not macro-enabled?
questions.e: The standard Excel workbook format in modern Office versions uses the .xlsx extension. A macro-enabled Excel workbook normally uses .xlsm, while .docx is a Word document and .pptx is a PowerPoint presentation.

questions.q: A persistent pollutant is present in small amounts in water but reaches a much higher concentration in top predatory fish. Which ecological process explains this increase across trophic levels?
questions.e: Biomagnification is the increase in concentration of a persistent substance at successively higher trophic levels in a food chain. Top predators may therefore accumulate much higher concentrations than organisms lower in the chain.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology, Class XII.

questions.q: In ecology, what does the term 'ecological niche' most accurately describe?
o: Only the physical shelter where an animal sleeps
The total number of species in a forest
The geographical coordinates of a protected area
A species' functional role, resource use and interactions within its ecosystem
questions.e: An ecological niche describes how a species functions within an ecosystem, including the resources it uses, the conditions it tolerates and its interactions with other organisms. It is broader than simply the physical place where the species is found.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology, Class XII.

questions.q: A forest absorbs more carbon dioxide from the atmosphere than it releases over a defined period. In climate science, the forest is functioning as a:
questions.e: A carbon sink removes or stores more carbon over a period than it releases. Forests and oceans can act as sinks, although their effectiveness depends on ecosystem condition, disturbance, land use and the time period considered.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NOAA — West Coast National Marine Sanctuaries, Blue Carbon Facts.

questions.q: What is the principal chemical cause of ocean acidification associated with rising atmospheric carbon dioxide?
o: Dissolved carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid and lowers seawater pH
Salt is converted directly into sulphuric acid
Ocean water becomes more alkaline because of evaporation
questions.e: Some atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater and reacts with water to form carbonic acid, which releases hydrogen ions and lowers pH. This chemical change can reduce the availability of carbonate ions needed by many shell-forming organisms.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NOAA — What is Ocean Acidification?.

questions.q: The ecological footprint of a population is intended to estimate:
o: The biologically productive land and water area needed to provide its resources and absorb its wastes
The number of endangered species in one national park
The height of the tallest tree in a forest
The annual rainfall of a city
questions.e: An ecological footprint estimates the biologically productive area required to supply the resources a population consumes and absorb the wastes it generates, under prevailing technology. It is an indicator of pressure on ecological capacity.

questions.q: In the ecosystem-services framework, pollination by insects that supports crop production is generally classified as which type of service?
questions.e: Pollination is generally classified as a regulating ecosystem service because organisms help regulate an essential ecological process. It supports crop production and wild-plant reproduction, but the service itself is the ecological regulation of pollination.

questions.q: Under India's Environmental Impact Assessment framework, why must listed development projects obtain prior environmental clearance before construction or land preparation begins?
o: To determine the market value of the project land
To certify that the project will make a profit
To examine potential environmental impacts and impose appropriate conditions before the project proceeds
To replace all local building permissions
questions.e: The EIA Notification 2006 requires prior environmental clearance for listed projects because their potential environmental impacts must be considered before construction or land preparation begins. The process allows the regulatory authority to assess proposals and set environmental conditions.

questions.topic: Ecosystem restoration — recovery of degraded systems
questions.q: Which action best matches the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration's meaning of ecosystem restoration?
o: Replacing every natural habitat with commercial plantations
Removing all human communities from every ecosystem
Increasing extraction of natural resources from degraded land
Assisting the recovery of ecosystems that have been degraded or destroyed
questions.e: Ecosystem restoration means assisting the recovery of ecosystems that have been degraded or destroyed. Actions may include restoring forests, rivers, wetlands, farmlands and coastal systems while supporting biodiversity and benefits to people.

questions.e: The Satyashodhak Samaj was established in 1873 and became associated with Jotirao Phule's challenge to caste hierarchy and social inequality. NCERT's Savitribai Phule memorial lecture also records the Samaj's initiative for marriages without priests, dowry and high costs.

questions.e: IGNOU's study material places the establishment of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra in 1867. It formed part of a wider nineteenth-century reform current addressing social and religious practices.

questions.topic: Constitutional history — Government of India Act 1858
questions.q: What major constitutional change followed the Government of India Act, 1858?
o: The administration of India was transferred from the East India Company to the British Crown
The Indian National Congress was created
questions.e: The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred the governance of India from the East India Company to the British Crown after the Revolt of 1857. It established direct Crown rule and created the office of Secretary of State for India.

questions.q: Which important change was made by the Charter Act of 1833?
o: The Governor-General of Bengal became the Governor-General of India
It transferred power to the Crown
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1833 centralised legislative authority and provided that the Governor-General of Bengal would become the Governor-General of India. Lord William Bentinck became the first holder of that office under the new arrangement.
